# Campaigns tools

Build audiences, review and launch campaigns (A/B, multilingual, scheduled), and optimize them live.

**OAuth scope:** `campaigns:send`, `campaigns:read` · **Tools:** 14 callable + 11 review-panel actions · **Approx. context cost:** ~10.3k tokens

| Tool | What it does | Action |
|---|---|---|
| [`preview_audience`](#preview_audience) | Quick look at an audience: count, columns and a masked sample. Nothing is saved. | Read-only |
| [`get_cdp_summary`](#get_cdp_summary) | Size of your customer data and the fields you can segment on, with value counts. | Read-only |
| [`clear_cdp_data`](#clear_cdp_data) | Permanently delete all customer-data profiles for the account. Irreversible; requires explicit confirmation. | **Deletes data** |
| [`resolve_audience`](#resolve_audience) | Save an audience server-side and get a handle for advanced sends and re-sends. | Writes |
| [`launch_campaign`](#launch_campaign) | Send or schedule a campaign on WhatsApp, RCS or SMS, for clones, re-sends and advanced flows. New campaigns go through the review panel. | **Sends messages** |
| [`pause_campaign`](#pause_campaign) | Pause a running campaign so queued messages stop. Already-submitted messages cannot be recalled. | Writes |
| [`get_campaign_status`](#get_campaign_status) | Where a campaign is: scheduled, queued, submitted, failed (with reason), cancelled or completed. | Read-only |
| [`optimize_running_campaign`](#optimize_running_campaign) | Health-check a live campaign and pause or reschedule it when delivery or failure thresholds are breached. Dry run first. | Writes |
| [`auto_fallback_channel`](#auto_fallback_channel) | Retry failed messages on the next channel in the campaign's policy (e.g. WhatsApp to SMS), respecting consent. | Writes |
| [`register_channel_fallback`](#register_channel_fallback) | Set up account-wide channel failover for a template (Smart CPaaS), covering API traffic too. | Writes |
| [`get_channel_fallback`](#get_channel_fallback) | Check whether channel failover is registered for a template. | Read-only |
| [`open_campaign_review`](#open_campaign_review) | Open the campaign review panel: preview each template, attach audiences, schedule, and launch after your confirmation. | Read-only |
| [`open_ab_test_review`](#open_ab_test_review) | Open the A/B test review panel: variants side by side, test on a sample, then send the winner to everyone else automatically. | Read-only |
| [`open_language_review`](#open_language_review) | Open the multilingual campaign panel: one card per language, and each recipient gets their language. | Read-only |

## `preview_audience`

Quick look at an audience: count, columns and a masked sample. Nothing is saved.

**Action:** Read-only

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audience_handle` **(required)** | `string` | Audience source to peek without persisting: cdp:all/segment, hubspot:all, hubspot:list:{id}, https URL, file path, or JSON. Bounded CRM preview only — no ap:{id}, no full pull. |
| `sample_size` | `integer` | Masked sample rows to return (default 5). |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Cheap audience peek — count, columns, masked sample only (no persist, no ap:{id}).

Use to sanity-check a segment or file before review. For the normal send path pass the spec
to open_campaign_review directly instead of calling resolve_audience first.

</details>

## `get_cdp_summary`

Size of your customer data and the fields you can segment on, with value counts.

**Action:** Read-only

_No parameters._

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Inspect the CDP audience before segmenting — sizes plus segmentable fields and their values.

Use when: user wants to target a segment (e.g. "at-risk customers", "high-value repeat buyers")
and you need to know which fields/values exist before calling resolve_audience with a cdp: filter.
Returns: total, opted_out, sendable, and segmentable_fields (each low-cardinality field mapped to
its distinct values with counts). Build a segment handle from these, e.g. cdp:churn_risk=at_risk,
then resolve_audience(cdp:...) → launch_campaign. Read-only.

</details>

Permanently delete all customer-data profiles for the account. Irreversible; requires explicit confirmation.

**Action:** **Deletes data**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `confirm` | `boolean` | Must be true. Only set after the user has explicitly confirmed deletion in chat. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Permanently delete ALL CDP profiles for this account (uploaded contacts and CRM mirrors).

DESTRUCTIVE and irreversible. Before calling: tell the user what will be deleted (use
get_cdp_summary for the count) and get an explicit yes. Call with confirm=true only then.

## `resolve_audience`

Save an audience server-side and get a handle for advanced sends and re-sends.

**Action:** Writes

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audience_handle` **(required)** | `string` | Audience source: cdp:all, cdp:segment (field<op>value; \| OR, & AND), hubspot:all, hubspot:list:{id}, export URL, file, or JSON. Returns ap:{id}. See get_cdp_summary for segment fields. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Persist audience server-side; return ap:{id}, count, columns, masked sample.

Use for advanced/direct sends, re-sends, or when you need ap:{id} before launch. For new

## `launch_campaign`

Send or schedule a campaign on WhatsApp, RCS or SMS, for clones, re-sends and advanced flows. New campaigns go through the review panel.

**Action:** **Sends messages** · **Channels:** WhatsApp, SMS, RCS

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audience_handle` **(required)** | `string` | Resolved handle from resolve_audience, format ap:{numeric_id}. Required. |
| `template_id` | `string` | Approved template id/code from Template MCP as a STRING — always quote it, even when purely numeric (e.g. "8652536", never the bare number 8652536). REQUIRED for RCS; optional for WhatsApp. For SMS this is the Gupshup DLT lookup id — pass it to auto-fetch the approved DLT template text and its real dltTemplateId/principalEntityId (see send_options). |
| `template_body` | `string` | Approved template text with variables (e.g. Hi {{first_name}}). Required for live WhatsApp bulk send; SMS sends it as the plain message text. Becomes the Gateway API msg field. When only template_id is known, leave this empty — the server fetches the approved body from the Gateway API automatically; never ask the user to paste it. |
| `variable_map` | `string`[] | Template variable column names from audience CSV, in placeholder order. |
| `channels` | `string`[] | Channel fallback chain, canonical order whatsapp -> rcs -> sms (default ["whatsapp"]). RCS requires template_id; SMS sends template_body as plain text. |
| `schedule_at` | `string` | ISO datetime to defer send (e.g. 2026-07-04T10:00:00). Omit or past = send now. |
| `budget_cap` | `number` | Max spend in default currency; audience trimmed by rate before submit. |
| `name` | `string` | Human-readable campaign label for dashboards. |
| `follow_ups` | `object`[] | Timed no-reply nudge waves: [{delay_hours, condition?, channel?, template_id?, variable_map?, message?}]. Not the same as channels fallback — see server instructions. |
| `send_options` | `object` | WhatsApp bulk API extras: is_template, header, footer, button_url_param, wa_template_json, media_url, media_id, media_msg_type (IMAGE\|DOCUMENT\|VIDEO), media_filename, text_msg_type (HSM\|TEXT). Text campaigns use XLSUPLOAD; media campaigns use MEDIA_MESSAGE_BULK_UPLOAD. wa_template_json is built per recipient from audience columns and only needs passing to override that: a limited-time offer reads COUPON_CODE and OFFER_EXPIRY (ISO or epoch-ms); a carousel reads CARD{n}_MEDIA_URL and CARD{n}_VAR{m} for up to 10 cards (n is 1-based; cards may have different variable counts but must share one media header and one button set), plus optional CARD{n}_QR{i} / CARD{n}_URL{i} for buttons taking a per-recipient value (i is the 0-based button index). SMS DLT extras: dlt_template_id, principal_entity_id — pass these when the user already gave them in chat. Not needed when template_id resolves via fetch (the fetched value wins if they disagree); required (here or in the uploaded CSV's dltTemplateId/principalEntityId columns) when it doesn't. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Send or schedule a campaign (whatsapp, rcs, or sms) from ap:{id}. Returns
campaign_id, status, recipients, follow_up_waves.

Use for clones, re-sends, and advanced flows — not new campaigns (open_campaign_review launches
via the panel). Background send when run_now; follow-up waves auto-fire.

</details>

|---|---|---|

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Pause a running campaign — stops unsent queued cohorts.

Use when: user wants to halt a send in progress or after optimize_running_campaign recommends pause.

## `optimize_running_campaign`

Health-check a live campaign and pause or reschedule it when delivery or failure thresholds are breached. Dry run first.

**Action:** Writes

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign_id` **(required)** | `string` | Running or paused campaign UUID to assess. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | True = report health/issues/recommendations only; False = apply pause/reschedule. |
| `auto_pause` | `boolean` | Override policy: pause on threshold breach. None = use campaign policy default. Ignored when the deployment disables auto-pause. |
| `delivery_rate_floor` | `number` | Min acceptable delivery rate 0–1 (e.g. 0.70). None = tenant default. |
| `failure_rate_ceiling` | `number` | Max acceptable failure rate 0–1 (e.g. 0.15). None = tenant default. |
| `reschedule_to` | `string` | ISO datetime to move unsent queued recipients to. Mutually exclusive with reschedule_hours_ahead. |
| `reschedule_hours_ahead` | `integer` | Reschedule queued recipients N hours from now. Alternative to reschedule_to. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Autonomously health-check a live campaign and pause or reschedule on threshold breach.

Use when: campaign is active and delivery/failure rates look off, or user asks to auto-tune a send.
Returns: campaign_id, health, issues[], actions_taken[], recommendations[], dry_run.
Workflow: call with dry_run=True first to preview, then dry_run=False to apply.
Use auto_fallback_channel for channel-level retries.

</details>

## `auto_fallback_channel`

Retry failed messages on the next channel in the campaign's policy (e.g. WhatsApp to SMS), respecting consent.

**Action:** Writes · **Channels:** WhatsApp, SMS, RCS

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign_id` **(required)** | `string` | Campaign with multi-channel policy (e.g. whatsapp then sms). |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | True = count eligible failures only; False = queue and submit fallback cohort. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Retry primary-channel failures on the next channel in the campaign policy (e.g. WhatsApp → SMS).

Use when: WhatsApp failures are high and campaign was launched with channels=["whatsapp","sms"].
Returns: primary_channel, fallback_channel, eligible_failures, queued_for_fallback,
skipped_no_consent, submitted, dry_run.
Only Gupshup fallback-eligible error codes are retried; respects CDP per-channel consent.
Distinct from launch_campaign's follow_ups: this retries an undelivered send within the
same wave, right away; follow_ups waits and nudges non-repliers on a timer, separately.

</details>

## `register_channel_fallback`

Set up account-wide channel failover for a template (Smart CPaaS), covering API traffic too.

**Action:** Writes · **Channels:** WhatsApp, SMS, RCS

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chain` **(required)** | `string` | Fallback chain to register: wa_sms (WhatsApp fails -> SMS), rcs_sms (RCS -> SMS), wa_rcs (redirect WhatsApp to RCS when the handset supports it), wa_rcs_sms (WhatsApp -> RCS, then SMS), rcs_wa_sms (RCS -> WhatsApp, then optional SMS). |
| `wa_template_id` | `string` | Numeric WhatsApp template id (htid) as a STRING (e.g. "8765325"). Required for wa_sms, wa_rcs, wa_rcs_sms; optional reference on rcs_wa_sms. |
| `rcs_template_code` | `string` | RCS template code. Required for every chain that touches RCS. |
| `sms_text` | `string` | SMS text for the terminal SMS leg. Placeholders are POSITIONAL on WA-source chains — {{1}} is the WA template's first body variable — and NAMED on RCS-source chains ({{code}} = the RCS customParams key). Raw JsonPath is rejected; the server generates the real paths itself. Required for wa_sms and rcs_sms; optional on rcs_wa_sms and wa_rcs_sms (omit = no SMS leg). |
| `sms_template_name` | `string` | Name label for the SMS leg. Required by rcs_sms, and by rcs_wa_sms when sms_text is given. |
| `dlt_template_id` | `string` | TRAI DLT content-template id of the SMS text (from the carrier DLT portal; every registered SMS template has one — see the Templates app's save_sms_dlt_template). Required whenever the chain has an SMS leg with sms_text. |
| `wa_msg_type` | `string` | WhatsApp template kind: TEXT (default) or MEDIA. Used by wa_sms, wa_rcs, wa_rcs_sms. |
| `whatsapp_json` | `string` | rcs_wa_sms only, required: full WhatsApp template message JSON for the WA leg. Any {{...}} inside must be simple RCS customParams names — raw JsonPath is rejected. |
| `whatsapp_template_name` | `string` | rcs_wa_sms only, required: name of the WhatsApp template used on the WA leg. |
| `variable_mappings` | `string` | wa_rcs and wa_rcs_sms, REQUIRED: JSON object mapping each RCS template variable to the WA body variable POSITION it copies, e.g. {"user": 1, "code": 2}. Integers only — the server generates the JsonPath and verifies the position exists on the real WA template. Ignored on other chains. |
| `custom_params` | `string` | wa_rcs / wa_rcs_sms optional: JSON object of static RCS template params (key = RCS variable name, value = fixed text). |
| `media_base_url` | `string` | wa_rcs / wa_rcs_sms with wa_msg_type=MEDIA: base URL for media assets. |
| `enterprise_account_id` | `string` | Numeric enterprise account id. Only needed when it cannot be derived from the connected WhatsApp gateway credentials. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Register platform-level channel failover for a template (Smart CPaaS).

Use when: the user wants failed or redirected sends to continue on the next
channel for ALL traffic on the account — including campaigns their CDP/CRM
fires through the Gupshup API, not only campaigns launched from this server.
The mapping is read by the platform send pipeline (Smart CPaaS); fallback
fires automatically once the account's matching feature flag and fallback
sender id are enabled (account-level config by Gupshup ops).

Required per chain:
- wa_sms:      wa_template_id, sms_text ({{1}}-style), dlt_template_id
- rcs_sms:     rcs_template_code, sms_text ({{name}}-style), sms_template_name, dlt_template_id
- wa_rcs:      wa_template_id, rcs_template_code, variable_mappings ({"rcsVar": position})
- wa_rcs_sms:  wa_template_id, rcs_template_code, variable_mappings; sms_text optional
- rcs_wa_sms:  rcs_template_code, whatsapp_json, whatsapp_template_name;
               optional SMS leg = sms_text + sms_template_name + dlt_template_id

Alignment is enforced, not trusted: on WA-source chains the tool fetches the
REAL approved template body, counts its variables, and refuses any reference
past that count. Raw JsonPath in any input is rejected — paths are generated
server-side. NOTE: editing the WA template later invalidates the mapping;
re-register after template changes.
Returns: ok, action (created|updated), chain, detail, note. Safe to re-run —
an existing mapping is updated in place.

</details>

## `open_campaign_review`

Open the campaign review panel: preview each template, attach audiences, schedule, and launch after your confirmation.

**Action:** Read-only · **Channels:** WhatsApp, SMS, RCS · **Opens panel:** `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review`

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` **(required)** | `string` | Campaign display name shown in the review panel and dashboards. |
| `segments_json` | `string` | JSON array of segment cards, one per template: [{"template_id": "8652536", "template_body": "", "audience_handle": ""}]. template_id REQUIRED per segment (always a quoted string). Leave template_body empty to auto-fetch the approved body from the Gateway API. audience_handle optional — the user can upload a userbase per card inside the panel. Max 10 segments. Omit ("") for a plain single-template call using the top-level params. |
| `audience_handle` | `string` | Single-template calls only: ap:{id} or raw spec (hubspot:all, hubspot:list:{id}, cdp:all, cdp:segment). OPTIONAL — pass it only when the user named a source in their request; otherwise leave it empty and the user uploads the userbase in the panel. Never default to cdp:all, and never ask which source to use. |
| `template_body` | `string` | Single-template calls only: approved template text with variables. Leave empty when only template_id is known — the server fetches the approved body automatically. NEVER ask the user to paste template text. |
| `channels` | `string` | Comma-separated channel chain from whatsapp/rcs/sms, applied to every segment. Pass the channel the USER chose. Never guess: a template id does not identify its channel, so a wrong guess sends a real campaign on the wrong channel. If the user named none, leave empty — the tool then returns error=channel_required naming the connected channels for you to ask about. RCS requires template_id. |
| `template_id` | `string` | Single-template calls only: approved template id/code as a STRING — always quote it (e.g. "8652536"). REQUIRED for RCS. For SMS this is the Gupshup DLT lookup id (not the DLT template id itself) — pass it to auto-fetch the approved DLT template text and its real dltTemplateId/principalEntityId. |
| `dlt_template_id` | `string` | SMS only: the DLT (India TRAI) template id, if the user already gave it in chat. Not needed when template_id resolves via fetch — the fetched value wins over this one if they disagree. Required (here or in the uploaded CSV's dltTemplateId column) when no template_id fetch resolves. |
| `principal_entity_id` | `string` | SMS only: the DLT principal entity id, if the user already gave it in chat. Not needed when template_id resolves via fetch. Required (here or in the uploaded CSV's principalEntityId column) when no template_id fetch resolves. |
| `follow_ups_json` | `string` | Single-template calls only: JSON follow-up waves. "" for single send. Not supported with segments_json. |
| `projected_impact` | `string` | Optional one-line projected impact, e.g. estimated conversions or revenue. |
| `audience_stats_json` | `string` | Optional aggregate stats JSON: {"highlights":[{"label","value"}],"breakdown":[{"label","count"}]}. Shown only on single-segment reviews. Real tool numbers only; "" if none. |
| `schedule_at` | `string` | Optional ISO date-time to schedule the send instead of sending on Launch, e.g. "2026-09-03T10:00:00+05:30" (include the user's UTC offset; a bare time is taken as UTC). Must be 2 minutes to 30 days ahead. Pre-fills the panel's schedule picker; the user can still change or clear it there. Leave "" to send on Launch. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

Required pre-flight panel before any new campaign — a carousel with one card per template.

Each card shows the template preview and lets the user attach that card's userbase
(in-card CSV/XLSX upload, or pass audience_handle per segment) and launch it. The footer
offers "1 userbase for all templates" (one CSV with a template_id mapping column,
partitioned server-side) and a Launch All gated on every card being ready. All card
launches group under ONE logical campaign; each is a separate bulk-send call. A plain
single-template call renders a one-card carousel. Wait for the user to Launch in the
panel — do NOT call launch_campaign yourself.

</details>

## `open_ab_test_review`

Open the A/B test review panel: variants side by side, test on a sample, then send the winner to everyone else automatically.

**Action:** Read-only · **Channels:** WhatsApp, SMS, RCS · **Opens panel:** `ui://gupshup-cpaas/ab-review`

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` **(required)** | `string` | Test display name; each variant's campaign is named '{name} [A]' etc. |
| `variants_json` **(required)** | `string` | JSON array of 2 (up to 3) variants: [{"label": "A", "channel": "whatsapp", "template_id": "8652536"}, {"label": "B", "channel": "whatsapp", "template_id": "8652540"}]. Pass the template_id the user named and leave template_body empty — the server fetches the approved body. Each variant needs a template_id or a template_body. Variants may vary copy and/or channel (whatsapp, rcs, sms); RCS variants require template_id. The audience needs only a PHONE column (plus %Var1..N when the templates have placeholders) — the server splits it and maps every recipient to its variant's template_id itself. |
| `audience_handle` | `string` | OPTIONAL — leave empty unless the user named a source in their request. Empty opens the panel with an empty audience card and the user uploads a CSV there (the default path). NEVER default to cdp:all and never ask the user which source to use — an unmentioned audience means 'upload in the panel'. Only when the user explicitly named one: an ap:{id} handle from resolve_audience, or a raw spec (hubspot:all, cdp:all, cdp:segment) previewed cheaply now and fully resolved once, on Launch. |
| `split_percent` | `integer` | Deprecated and ignored. The sample is always dealt evenly across the variants. |
| `sample_percent` | `integer` | Share of the audience that is the TEST (default 10, i.e. 10%). The sampled recipients are dealt evenly across the variants; everyone else is held out and receives the winning template automatically after evaluate_after_hours. Pass only when the user named a different share (1-50). |
| `sample_cap` | `integer` | Maximum recipients in the test sample (default 1000). Pass only when the user named one. |
| `evaluate_after_hours` | `number` | Hours after the test is sent before the winner is decided and sent to the holdout (default 24). Pass only when the user named a different window. |
| `winner_metric` | `string` | How the winner is judged: clicks_then_reads (default: click rate when any variant gets clicks, otherwise read rate), click_rate, read_rate, or delivery_rate. Pass only when the user named the criterion; the panel has a 'Winner by' control where they can change it before Launch. click_rate is refused (winner_metric_not_applicable) unless EVERY variant's template has a button or link to click -- offer reads or delivered instead. |
| `channels` | `string` | Optional comma-separated channels for the header display (whatsapp/rcs/sms). |
| `follow_ups_json` | `string` | Reserved for parity with open_campaign_review; not yet used per-variant. |
| `projected_impact` | `string` | Optional one-line projected impact. |
| `audience_stats_json` | `string` | Optional aggregate CRM stats, same shape as open_campaign_review. |
| `schedule_at` | `string` | Optional ISO date-time to schedule the send instead of sending on Launch, e.g. "2026-09-03T10:00:00+05:30" (include the user's UTC offset; a bare time is taken as UTC). Must be 2 minutes to 30 days ahead. Pre-fills the panel's schedule picker; the user can still change or clear it there. Leave "" to send on Launch. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

REQUIRED for any A/B or split test of campaign copy/channels — never launch variants
yourself via launch_campaign directly.

Opens a pre-flight review panel showing each variant's bubble side by side with the shared
audience, then on Launch sends the test to a SAMPLE of the audience: 10% by default, at
most 1000 recipients, dealt evenly across the variants by hash(msisdn) so cohorts never
overlap and a retried launch reproduces the same split. Everyone else is held out. After
evaluate_after_hours (default 24) the server reads Gupshup's campaign stats for each
variant, picks the winner (click rate when any variant registered clicks, otherwise read
rate) and sends the winning template to the held-out recipients automatically -- nothing
for the agent or the user to do. get_campaign_status(logical id or any variant campaign
id) reports the test's state: testing (and when it is judged), promoted (winner, metric,
the holdout campaign), inconclusive, or failed. A file that already carries a template_id
column keeps its own mapping: the whole audience is the test and nothing is promoted.
Returns (structuredContent): review_session_id, count, recipient_count, variants (each with
its own recipient_count), ab_plan (mode, sample_size, holdout_count, evaluate_after_hours),
resolution ("immediate" | "at_launch"), launch_gate.

</details>

| `variants_json` **(required)** | `string` | JSON array of language variants, YOU write each language's copy: [{"language": "Hindi", "language_code": "hi", "template_body": "...", "button_label": "..."}, {"language": "English", "template_body": "..."}]. |
| `audience_handle` | `string` | OPTIONAL — leave empty unless the user named a source in their request. Empty opens the panel with an empty audience card and the user uploads a CSV there (the default path). NEVER default to cdp:all and never ask the user which source to use — an unmentioned audience means 'upload in the panel'. Only when the user explicitly named one: an ap:{id} handle from resolve_audience, or a raw spec (hubspot:all, cdp:all, cdp:segment) previewed cheaply now and fully resolved once, on Launch. |
| `channels` | `string` | Comma-separated channels shared by every language variant (whatsapp/rcs/sms, default "whatsapp"). |
| `projected_impact` | `string` | Optional one-line projected impact. |
| `schedule_at` | `string` | Optional ISO date-time to schedule the send instead of sending on Launch, e.g. "2026-09-03T10:00:00+05:30" (include the user's UTC offset; a bare time is taken as UTC). Must be 2 minutes to 30 days ahead. Pre-fills the panel's schedule picker; the user can still change or clear it there. Leave "" to send on Launch. |

<details><summary>Model-facing description</summary>

REQUIRED when the user wants a campaign in multiple languages / localized copy. The AI
writes each language's template_body itself before calling this.

Opens a pre-flight review panel with one bubble card per language and launches ONE campaign
per language on Launch (never launch_campaign directly). Recipients are partitioned by their
CDP/variables language field (matched on language_code or name, case-insensitive); recipients
with no or unrecognized language go to the FIRST variant in variants_json — list your most
common language first.
Returns (structuredContent): review_session_id, count, languages, variants,
distribution_known (whether per-language counts are exact or an even-split display estimate),
resolution ("immediate" | "at_launch").

</details>

## Review-panel actions

These tools are called by the interactive review panel (MCP Apps) when you click in it. They are not offered to the model, and clients that don't render panels never call them.

| Tool | Panel | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `upload_audience_file` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: attach an uploaded CSV/XLSX audience. |
| `attach_segment_audience` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: attach an audience to one template card. |
| `set_shared_audience` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: use one audience file for all templates. |
| `detach_segment_audience` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: remove a card's audience. |
| `set_campaign_schedule` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: schedule the campaign. |
| `cancel_campaign_schedule` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: cancel a schedule. |
| `get_review_panel_state` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: load the panel's current state. |
| `get_review_status` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: poll launch progress. |
| `attach_review_audience` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: attach an audience to the review. |
| `confirm_campaign_launch` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/campaign-segments-review` | Review panel: the user's Launch click, which sends the campaign. |
| `set_ab_winner_metric` | `ui://gupshup-cpaas/ab-review` | A/B panel: choose the winner metric (click rate or read rate). |
